title: "Flag differences in NRT"
format:
  html:

execute:

What is left after the Depth and Delayed mode pages: profiles at sea,
marked NRT, and not estimated to carry delayed mode flags. The estimate is
made per variable, so each variable is counted over its own profiles: one
whose salinity looks reworked by an operator is in the temperature figures
and not in the salinity ones. Both flags on them should come from automated
tests, so where they disagree, the tests differ. Either one side runs a test
the other does not, or both run it with different logic or thresholds.

This page compares the two sides. The next two take each side of a
disagreement in turn, because they can be read to different depths:

- [Flagged only by the input](analyses-flags-original.qmd): the input
  carries one flag per variable and nothing about how it was reached, so
  these are described by where they sit in their profiles, the value the
  input gave them, and the tests the producers say they run that nrtqclib
  does not.
- [Flagged only by nrtqclib](analyses-flags-nrtqclib.qmd): nrtqclib records
  which of its checks failed, so these can be traced to the checks behind
  them, and set against whether the producer runs the same test and how
  the two designs of a test can differ.

```{ojs}
//| output: false
app = import(new URL("assets/js/app.js", document.baseURI).href)
meta = app.loadAnalyses()
name = (id) => app.datasetName(meta, id)
table = app.analysisTable
byDataset = (a, b) => app.datasetOrder(meta, a.dataset_id) - app.datasetOrder(meta, b.dataset_id)
variableLabel = (n) => meta.variables.find((v) => v.name === n)?.label ?? n
variableOrder = (n) => meta.variables.findIndex((v) => v.name === n)
byDatasetVariable = (a, b) => byDataset(a, b) || variableOrder(a.variable) - variableOrder(b.variable)
status = meta ? app.loadAnalysisTable("items_status") : null
totals = new Map((status ?? []).reduce((m, r) => {
  const key = `${r.dataset_id}|${r.variable}`;
  m.set(key, (m.get(key) ?? 0) + r.n_obs);
  return m;
}, new Map()))
```

```{ojs}
meta === null ? app.analysesMissing() : html``
```

## What each side runs

nrtqclib runs the same checks on every product. The input's tests are the
producer's. The Arctic, Baltic and Mediterranean regional centres said which
near real time tests they run on CTD profiles; the table sets their answers
beside nrtqclib's checks. The answers describe the regional products only:
the global products' flags come from the global product's own QC, which
they do not describe.

Under an answer, in grey, is what the input flags show of it: the share of
the clear failures of nrtqclib's version of the test that the input flags,
per variable, per flag, or for density per level and per dbar,
explained in [What the input flags show](#what-the-input-flags-show). Near
100% means the producer runs the test; near 0 means it does not, or only
with a far larger threshold. "Too few" is a test with too few clear
failures in the product to tell.

```{ojs}
response = meta ? app.loadAnalysisTable("items_response") : null
seenText = (datasetId, test) => {
  if (!response) return "";
  const parts = test.response.flatMap((key) => {
    const rows = app.clearFailures(response, meta, datasetId, key);
    const what = (r) => key === "density_inversion" ? "per level"
      : key === "density_inversion_per_dbar" ? "per dbar"
      : app.responseFlagLabel(meta, r.variable);
    return rows.map((r) => `${what(r)} ${r.share === null ? "too few" : app.formatPercent(100 * r.share)}`);
  });
  return parts.length ? `flags: ${parts.join(", ")}` : "";
}
claimCell = (datasetId) => (_, row) => {
  const cell = document.createElement("span");
  cell.append(row.claims[datasetId]);
  const seen = seenText(datasetId, row);
  if (seen) {
    const note = document.createElement("span");
    note.className = "nq-seen";
    note.textContent = seen;
    cell.append(note);
  }
  return cell;
}
claimsTable = {
  const box = table(app.REGIONAL_TESTS, [
    { key: "label", label: "Test", align: "left", wrap: true, format: (v) => v },
    { key: "nrtqclib", label: "nrtqclib", align: "left", format: (v) => v },
    ...app.REGIONAL_PRODUCTS.map((p) => ({
      key: p.id, label: p.label, align: "left", wrap: true, render: claimCell(p.id)
    }))
  ]);
  box.classList.add("nq-claims");
  return box;
}
```

"Not asked" is a test the centres were not asked about and did not
mention. The frozen profile test is listed by all three, but leaves no
sign in their flags: none of them flags an exact repeat of a platform's
previous profile, measured as described below, though only the Arctic has
enough of them to tell. See also
[Flagged only by the input](analyses-flags-original.qmd#tests-nrtqclib-does-not-have).
A test both sides run can still disagree: the
[nrtqclib page](analyses-flags-nrtqclib.qmd#how-one-test-can-differ)
describes how.

## What the input flags show

A producer may run a test it does not list, or list one that has no effect
on its flags. To see which, every failure of a test is measured again from
the values, the way nrtqclib's check does it, and put in a band by how far
past nrtqclib's threshold it is; then the share of each band the input
flags is counted. A producer that runs the test flags nearly all of the
failures far past the threshold, and starts flagging where its own
threshold lies. One that does not run it flags them about as often as any
other observation, well under 1%.

The tests are measured over the same profiles as the rest of this page.
Spike and gradient are measured on values inside the global range, and
gradient only on levels that pass the spike test, so that one test is not
taken for another; stuck value and density inversion likewise only on
values inside the range. Density is the density at the surface from the
in situ temperature, close to but not the same as nrtqclib's potential
density, and the centres' threshold is per dbar, so both are shown. A
stuck profile is counted as flagged when the input flags nearly all of its
values.

nrtqclib has no frozen profile test, so it is measured the way the Argo
real time QC manual describes it: each profile is set against the same
platform's previous one at another time, by the means of 50 dbar slabs.
Moorings and ice-tethered profilers profile hours apart, and many of
their profiles pass Argo's limits without anything being wrong, so only
an exact repeat, the same pressures and values at every level, counts as a
clear failure. Like stuck value, it is measured only on profiles inside the
range and not one value throughout, and a profile counts as flagged when
the input flags nearly all of its values.

```{ojs}
meta ? app.analysisFigure(
  "items_response",
  "The share of each test's failures the input flags, by how far past nrtqclib's threshold they are. One panel per test and the flag it is set against; a band with fewer than 20 failures is left out. Colour is the product and line type the region.",
  "Line charts per test of the share flagged by the input against the size of the failure, one line per product."
) : html``
```

The bands of one product, with how many failures each holds.

```{ojs}

  ? Inputs.select([...new Set(response.map((r) => r.dataset_id))], { label: "Product", format: name })
  : html``
```

```{ojs}
meta && response ? table(
  response
    .filter((r) => r.dataset_id === responseDataset)
    .map((r) => {
      const test = meta.response_tests.find((t) => t.key === r.test);
      return {
        ...r,
        key: `${r.test}|${r.variable}|${r.band}`,
        test_label: test.label,
        flag: app.responseFlagLabel(meta, r.variable),
        band_label: test.bands[r.band].label,
        clear: test.clear.includes(r.band) ? "clear" : "",
        unit: test.unit
      };
    }),
  [
    { key: "test_label", label: "Test", align: "left", format: (v) => v },
    { key: "flag", label: "Set against", align: "left", format: (v) => v },
    { key: "band_label", label: "How far past", align: "left", format: (v) => v },
    { key: "clear", label: "Clear failure", align: "left", format: (v) => v },
    { key: "n", label: "Failures", title: "Observations, pairs of levels or profiles, as the test counts them" },
    { key: "n_flagged", label: "The input flags", format: (v, r) => app.formatSmallShare(v, r.n) }
  ]
) : html``
```

Read together, for the regional products whose centres answered:

- **Arctic NRT regional**: global range and spike behave as claimed: the
  input flags nearly all of their clear failures, from about nrtqclib's
  thresholds. Gradient mostly, about four in five. Density inversion runs
  on the ice-tethered profilers only, and not as described: on them the
  input flags the deeper level of nearly every pair of levels whose
  potential density falls by 0.05 kg/m³ or more, and almost none below,
  so the threshold is 0.05 between levels rather than per dbar. The other
  platforms flag almost none of their inversions, which is why only about
  a quarter of the clear inversions are flagged
  ([by platform](#density-inversion-by-platform)). There are too few stuck
  profiles to tell. The input flags none of the exact repeats of a
  platform's previous profile, so the frozen profile test it lists leaves
  no sign.
- **Baltic NRT regional**: gradient and stuck value leave no sign, as the
  centre says it runs neither. Spike and density inversion, which it says
  it runs, leave almost none either: the input flags almost none of the
  clear salinity spikes (there are too few clear temperature spikes to
  tell), and most of its platforms flag no inversion of any size. The
  platforms that flag most of their clear inversions hold about 1% of
  them, too few to place the threshold
  ([by platform](#density-inversion-by-platform)). Salinity just under nrtqclib's lower
  bound of 2 is mostly flagged, which fits a range test with a bound near
  it. There are too few exact repeats of a platform's previous profile to
  tell whether its frozen profile test runs.
- **Mediterranean NRT regional**: too few clear failures to tell for most
  tests. The input flags a sixth of the few clear density inversions,
  although the centre says the test is not run yet; another test may
  account for them.

ctddump sorts each profile by pressure when it converts it
([Data conversion](analyses-conversion.qmd#pressure-order)), so no profile
in these data goes shallower, and the only failures of pressure increasing
are repeated pressures. The Baltic input leaves those unflagged, which fits
a test that fails only a pressure going shallower. The Baltic source files
do hold profiles that go back up, but the sort has hidden them, so whether
its test runs cannot be seen here. Of the global
products, the Mediterranean one flags more than half of the repeated
pressures, but in its pressure flag rather than in temperature or salinity,
which this site compares.

### Density inversion by platform

A density test run on some platforms only shows in its flags on those
platforms alone, so the inversions are counted again per platform group
(ice-tethered profilers, whose codes start `ITP-` or `TOP-`, and the
rest) in finer bands around 0.05 kg/m³, and per platform. The density is
the same as above. Since a test flags the deeper or the upper level of a
pair, the two are counted apart for the ice-tethered profilers; for the
other platforms the table counts a flag at either level.

- **Arctic NRT regional**: on the ice-tethered profilers the input flags
  the deeper level of 6% of the inversions from 0.0495 to 0.05 kg/m³
  between levels, 97% from 0.05 to 0.0505, and all of those above: a test
  at 0.05 kg/m³ between levels. Per dbar there is no such step, since
  their levels are 1 to 2 dbar apart. The upper level is flagged in a
  quarter to over half of the pairs, more often the larger the inversion.
  The other platforms, mostly ships, flag 0.1% of their inversions from
  0.05 to 0.2 kg/m³ and 13% of the larger ones, which other tests can
  account for; two of them flag nearly all of their few clear ones. They
  hold three quarters of the clear inversions, which is why only about a
  quarter of those are flagged over the whole product.
- **Baltic NRT regional**: 413 of the 521 platforms with a clear inversion
  flag none of them, and they hold 90% of the clear inversions. 61
  platforms flag at least half of theirs, and they hold 1%: most have
  fewer than ten each, too few to place a threshold, and only seven have
  ten or more, which they nearly all flag. Of their inversions up to 0.05
  kg/m³ they flag 1.5%.

```{ojs}
densityThreshold = meta ? app.loadAnalysisTable("density_threshold") : null
densityPlatforms = meta ? app.loadAnalysisTable("density_platforms") : null
densityGroupLabel = (g) => g === "ice_tethered" ? "Ice-tethered profilers" : "Other platforms"
densityBand = (r) => r.upper === null ? `More than ${r.lower}` : `${r.lower} to ${r.upper}`
viewof densityDataset = densityThreshold
  ? Inputs.select([...new Set(densityThreshold.map((r) => r.dataset_id))], {
      label: "Product", format: name,
      value: densityThreshold.some((r) => r.dataset_id === "ar_ar") ? "ar_ar" : undefined
    })
  : html`<p class="nq-empty">This data release has no density by platform tables.</p>`
viewof densityMeasure = densityThreshold
  ? Inputs.radio(new Map([["Between levels", "level"], ["Per dbar", "dbar"]]), {
      label: "Inversion", value: "level"
    })
  : html``
```

```{ojs}
densityThreshold ? (() => {
  const rows = densityThreshold.filter(
    (r) => r.dataset_id === densityDataset && r.measure === densityMeasure
  );
  const bands = [...new Map(rows.map((r) => [r.band, r])).values()].sort((a, b) => a.band - b.band);
  const cell = (band, group) => rows.find((r) => r.band === band && r.platform_group === group);
  return table(
    bands.map((b) => {
      const tethered = cell(b.band, "ice_tethered");
      const other = cell(b.band, "other");
      return {
        band: densityBand(b),
        t_n: tethered?.n ?? 0,
        t_deeper: tethered ? app.formatSmallShare(tethered.n_flagged_deeper, tethered.n) : "",
        t_upper: tethered ? app.formatSmallShare(tethered.n_flagged_upper, tethered.n) : "",
        o_n: other?.n ?? 0,
        o_either: other ? app.formatSmallShare(other.n_flagged, other.n) : ""
      };
    }),
    [
      { key: "band", label: densityMeasure === "level" ? "Inversion, kg/m³" : "Inversion, kg/m³ per dbar", align: "left", format: (v) => v },
      { key: "t_n", label: "Ice-tethered: pairs" },
      { key: "t_deeper", label: "Deeper level flagged", format: (v) => v },
      { key: "t_upper", label: "Upper level flagged", format: (v) => v },
      { key: "o_n", label: "Other: pairs" },
      { key: "o_either", label: "Either level flagged", format: (v) => v }
    ]
  );
})() : html``
```

The platforms of the product with an inversion above 0.05 kg/m³ between
levels, those with the most first.

    { key: "n_small", label: "Inversions up to 0.05" },

## By platform

The platforms of one product, with the share of their observations each
side alone flags. Sort by a column to find the platforms a disagreement
comes from; the [Platforms](platforms.qmd) page opens their profiles.

```{ojs}
platforms = meta ? app.loadAnalysisTable("items_platforms") : null
viewof platformDataset = meta && platforms
  ? Inputs.select([...new Set(platforms.map((r) => r.dataset_id))], { label: "Product", format: name })
  : html``
```

```{ojs}
// One row per platform, each variable's counts over its own NRT profiles.
// The shares are kept as percentages so the columns sort by value.
share = (part, whole) => (whole > 0 ? (100 * part) / whole : null)
platformRows = platforms
  ? [...platforms
      .filter((r) => r.dataset_id === platformDataset)
      .reduce((m, r) => {
        const row = m.get(r.platform_code) ?? { key: r.platform_code, platform_code: r.platform_code };
        row[`${r.variable}_profiles`] = r.n_profiles;
        row[`${r.variable}_obs`] = r.n_obs;
        row[`${r.variable}_oo`] = share(r.n_original_only, r.n_obs);
        row[`${r.variable}_no`] = share(r.n_nrtqclib_only, r.n_obs);
        m.set(r.platform_code, row);
        return m;
      }, new Map()).values()]
  : []
meta && platforms ? table(
  platformRows,
  [
    { key: "platform_code", label: "Platform", align: "left", format: (v) => v },
    ...meta.variables.flatMap((v) => [
      { key: `${v.name}_profiles`, label: `${v.label}: profiles`, format: (x) => (x == null ? "" : app.formatCount(x)) },
      { key: `${v.name}_oo`, label: "Original only", format: app.formatPercent },
      { key: `${v.name}_no`, label: "nrtqclib only", format: app.formatPercent }
    ])
  ],
  { sortKey: `${meta.variables[0].name}_profiles`, descending: true }
) : html``
```

## Against CORA's delayed mode flags

Machine learning for QC trains on delayed mode flags, so the question for
the NRT flags is how close they come to them. CORA holds many of the NRT
products' casts again, with delayed mode flags, and the
[Data conversion](analyses-conversion.qmd) page pairs them. Here a pair is
compared level by level when both copies hold the same levels: the same
number of observations, the same observation numbers, and pressures within
0.1 dbar at every level. As everywhere on this page, a variable is counted
only over the profiles that are NRT for it. Each level then carries four
flags: the producer's NRT flag, nrtqclib's on the NRT copy, CORA's, and
nrtqclib's on the CORA copy.

The pairs, through each condition, for the casts under the same platform
code in both products:

```{ojs}
coraPairs = meta ? app.loadAnalysisTable("cora_pairs") : null
coraFlags = meta ? app.loadAnalysisTable("cora_flags") : null
coraPairs ? table(
  coraPairs.filter((r) => r.coverage === "same_platform").sort(byDatasetVariable),
  [
    { key: "dataset_id", label: "Product", align: "left", format: name },
    { key: "variable", label: "Variable", align: "left", format: variableLabel },
    { key: "n_pairs", label: "Pairs" },
    { key: "n_same_obs", label: "Same number of levels" },
    { key: "n_nrt", label: "NRT for the variable" },
    { key: "n_aligned", label: "Same levels", title: "The same observation numbers, pressures within 0.1 dbar" },
    { key: "n_obs", label: "Levels compared" }
  ]
) : html`<p class="nq-empty">This data release has no comparison with CORA.</p>`
```

How far each set of flags agrees with CORA's. An observation is counted
when the producer's flag and CORA's both say something (neither missing,
0 nor 9). Flags 3, 4, 6 and 7 are bad for the producer and CORA, as on the
rest of the site, and any flag above 1 for nrtqclib. Kappa is Cohen's: 1
when the two agree on every observation, 0 when they agree no more often
than chance would. "Of CORA's" is the share of the observations CORA flags
that the other source flags too.

- **Baltic and Mediterranean NRT regional**: CORA's flags are the
  producer's, value for value, on every level compared, and nrtqclib's flags
  on the two copies agree as closely. CORA holds these casts with the NRT
  flags unchanged, so they say nothing about how close the NRT flags come
  to a delayed mode QC.
- **Arctic NRT regional**: CORA flags far more than the producer, 12% of
  the salinity against 1.4%, and nearly all the salinity the producer flags
  CORA flags too. nrtqclib flags the two copies differently on about 1% of
  their levels, so the CORA copy is not the NRT copy with new flags, and its
  flags on the CORA copy come closer to CORA's, for temperature most.
- **The global product**: the producer's flags are close to CORA's (kappa
  0.68 to 0.99), and nrtqclib's are not (below 0.15), since it flags several
  times more.

```{ojs}
coraAgreement = coraFlags ? (() => {
  const bad = (flag, values) => flag !== null && values.includes(flag);
  const groups = new Map();
  for (const r of coraFlags) {
    if (r.coverage !== "same_platform") continue;
    const v = meta.variables.find((x) => x.name === r.variable);
    const says = (f) => f !== null && !v.missing_flag_values.includes(f);
    if (!says(r.original_flag) || !says(r.cora_flag)) continue;
    const key = `${r.dataset_id}|${r.variable}`;
    const g = groups.get(key) ?? {
      dataset_id: r.dataset_id, variable: r.variable, n: 0, c: 0,
      sources: { p: [0, 0], n: [0, 0], m: [0, 0] }
    };
    const c = bad(r.cora_flag, v.bad_flag_values);
    const flagged = {
      p: bad(r.original_flag, v.bad_flag_values),
      n: r.nrtqclib_flag > 1,
      m: r.cora_nrtqclib_flag > 1
    };
    g.n += r.n_obs;
    if (c) g.c += r.n_obs;
    // Per source: how many it flags, and how many of those CORA flags too.
    for (const [s, f] of Object.entries(flagged)) {
      if (f) g.sources[s][0] += r.n_obs;
      if (f && c) g.sources[s][1] += r.n_obs;
    }
    groups.set(key, g);
  }
  const kappa = (n, c, f, both) => {
    const observed = (both + (n - f - c + both)) / n;
    const chance = (f * c + (n - f) * (n - c)) / (n * n);
    return chance === 1 ? null : (observed - chance) / (1 - chance);
  };
  return [...groups.values()].map((g) => {
    const row = { dataset_id: g.dataset_id, variable: g.variable, n: g.n, cora: (100 * g.c) / g.n };
    for (const [s, [f, both]] of Object.entries(g.sources)) {
      row[`${s}_share`] = (100 * f) / g.n;
      row[`${s}_kappa`] = kappa(g.n, g.c, f, both);
      row[`${s}_recall`] = g.c ? (100 * both) / g.c : null;
    }
    return row;
  }).sort(byDatasetVariable);
})() : []
formatKappa = (v) => (v === null || v === undefined ? "" : v.toFixed(2))
coraFlags ? table(coraAgreement, [
  { key: "dataset_id", label: "Product", align: "left", format: name },
  { key: "variable", label: "Variable", align: "left", format: variableLabel },
  { key: "n", label: "Observations" },
  { key: "cora", label: "CORA flags", format: app.formatPercent },
  { key: "p_share", label: "Producer flags", format: app.formatPercent },
  { key: "p_recall", label: "Of CORA's", format: app.formatPercent },
  { key: "p_kappa", label: "Kappa", format: formatKappa },
  { key: "n_share", label: "nrtqclib flags", format: app.formatPercent },
  { key: "n_recall", label: "Of CORA's", format: app.formatPercent },
  { key: "n_kappa", label: "Kappa", format: formatKappa },
  { key: "m_kappa", label: "nrtqclib on CORA: kappa", format: formatKappa, title: "nrtqclib's flags on the CORA copy against CORA's" }
]) : html``
```
